In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the cross section of Higgs boson production in the Standard Model of particle physics at the Large Hadton Collider (LHC), the most powerful particle accelerator ever built.
the theoretical study of the production of a Higgs boson via gluon fusion in hadronic collisions, at Next-to-Next-To-Leading-Logarithmic (NNLL) accuracy in QCD.
the theoretical study of the production of a Higgs boson (with a mass of 120 GeV) at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the LHC, the soft-gluon corrections at NNLL accuracy are very important in the low-q_T region, and that the inclusion of the NLO corrections is essential in the intermediate region (q_T of the order of M_H).

, for the LHC, the soft-gluon-resummed predictions for the Higgs transverse-momentum distribution are in good agreement with NLO fixed-order ones for q_T ~ 100 GeV, and that the resummation is needed to improve the theoretical accuracy of the fixed-order results for smaller q_T values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NNLO+NNLL predictions are in good agreement with the LHC data, and they are in general much closer to the data than the NLO+NNLL results.
we have computed the Higgs differential distributions for the most general case, i.e. we have included the effects of both top and bottom quark Yukawa couplings.

, for q_T ~ M_H and y ~ 0, the NNLL results for the q_T and y distributions of the Higg boson agree very well with the NLO results for q_T ~ 100 GeV and y ~ 2.5, and are about 10% higher than the NLO results at q_T ~ 200 GeV and y = 1.5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the LHC, the resummed results are not very different from the fixed-order ones.
soft-gluon effects are very important for the Higgs production cross section at the LHC.

, for the LHC, the resummed predictions for the Higgs q_T and y distributions are very close to the fixed-order NLO ones, and the inclusion of the soft-gluon corrections is therefore of little relevance.
